results.summary: Rapid Response Grants
results.content: Rapid Response Grants

beneficiaryAdministration:
The objective of the Call for rapid response grants is to support:

  1. activities to ensure that groups at risk of discrimination, unequal treatment, hate speech and hate crimes (in particular LGBT+ people, women, people with disabilities, Roma, people with migration experience) enjoy the rights guaranteed by the Charter of Fundamental Rights; and
  2. evidence-based advocacy, watchdog and monitoring activities that support respect for the rule of law.

Total budget for the call: PLN 1 329 805 (approx. EUR 312 673)

Minimum/maximum grant amount: PLN 20 000-40 000 (approx. EUR 4 700 - 9 300)

In order to be eligible, applicants must:

  1. Be established in Poland.
  2. Be non-profit making and a civil society organisation.
  3. Respect EU values as laid down in Art.2 of the Treaty on European Union and the EU Charter of fundamental rights. 
  4. Have eligible legal form: foundations, associations registered in the National Court Register, church legal persons registered in the National Court Register, rural housewives’ circles, unions of associations 

Only activities taking place in an EU Member State are eligible. 

Submitted proposals will be evaluated by the Equal Rights Project team in an internal, one-stage process. The team has the necessary knowledge and experience of the subject of the call. 

Grants will be awarded a maximum of five times (until the allocation is exhausted), according to the following schedule: • until December 15, 2025; • until February 15, 2026; • until April 15, 2026; • until July 15, 2026; • until October 15 2026. 

Eligible types of project activities: 

  1. watchdog and monitoring activities; 
  2. advocacy campaigns; 
  3. developing research and analysis for advocacy purposes; 
  4. countering disinformation and fact-checking; 
  5. developing and testing models, methods and interventions;  
  6. networking; 
  7. developing and managing platforms for cooperation between civil society organisations; 
  8. activities to strengthen the organisation in the event of a sudden loss of financial resources; 
  9. activities supporting the team in situations of overload and burnout. 

Organisations cannot conduct religious worship as part of the project, and funded activities must not directly or indirectly promote religious doctrine, mission or appeal to a particular faith. 

Further information, including a detailed description of the call procedure, can be found on the Equal Rights Programme website: https://programrownychpraw.batory.org.pl/.

results.summary: Call for CSOs initiatives “Code Success” Fund
results.content: Call for CSOs initiatives “Code Success” Fund

beneficiaryAdministration:
The submission of proposals is entirely web-based. For this purpose, the applicant must be pre-registered in the Electronic Proposal Submission System (EPSS). Access to the EPSS is via the PACT project website: https://pact.osis.bg. The form is completed in Bulgarian in EPSS. The form is submitted in EPSS along with the mandatory attachments.

The submission and assessment process will follow a two-stage procedure.

Stage 1 – Concept Note submission (16 February 2026 – 20 April 2026)

The call for proposals will be published on the PACT Project’s website as well as the websites of PACT Consortium partners.

Eligibility check and notification of eligible applicants (20-27 April 2026)

WCIF will conduct an administrative check for all submissions to ensure compliance with eligibility and formal criteria before quality assessment. All candidates will be informed by email about the results of the administrative compliance check, and only proposals of concept notes that have passed it will be admitted to the quality assessment.

Quality assessment of the concept notes (27 April 2026 – 1 June 2026)

The quality assessment of the concept notes will be done by two impartial and working independently from each other evaluators, at least one of whom is external to WCIF.

A ranked concept notes’ list, together with recommendations for changes (if any) to the proposed budgets of the ranked proposals, will be submitted by WCIF to the Initiative Selection Committee (ISC) for consideration. Subsequently the ISC provides WCIF with a list of the concept notes it has approved, considering their ranking by points and the available budget.

Only applicants with approved concept notes will be eligible to submit full proposals for initiatives. All applicants with assessed concept notes will be informed by email about the assessment results of the Concept Note stage and whether they proceed to the Full Proposal phase.

Stage 2 – Full Proposal submission (1 June 2026 – 3 August 2026)

Shortlisted applicants will be invited to submit their full proposals.

In the first half of June 2026, during the period of preparation of full proposals all organizations with approved concept notes will receive capacity building support.

Assessment and contracting (3 August 2026 – 30 September 2026)

The quality assessment will be carried out by WCIF. Based on the results of the assessment results, the WCIF team ranks all submitted proposals. The ranking is reviewed by the Initiative Selection Committee, which makes the final selection of proposals for initiatives. All applicants at Stage 2 will be informed by email about the final selection.

Project implementation start (September – October 2026)
description:
The Code Success Fund will support initiatives that raise awareness of EU rights and values, promote democracy and active civic participation, protect media freedom and counter disinformation, and work for equality, inclusion, and non-discrimination.

The supported initiatives may include:

-Awareness raising, including communication and information campaigns,

-Activities aimed at countering disinformation regarding EU values and policies,

-Various activities fostering civic dialogues at local level on topics related to EU rights and values,

-Activities in the local community to create coalitions and partnerships between civil society organizations,

-Civic participation/advocacy with the aim of contributing to decision-making processes (at regional or local level),

-Training, exchange of experience and good practices, mentoring, knowledge transfer, and other activities aimed at increasing the capacity of civil society organizations and other stakeholders on topics related to EU values,

-Activities that promote interethnic and intercultural dialogue in the community

-Providing free advice and monitoring implementation of EU policies, rights, and values at the local level in accordance with the EU Treaties and the Charter of Fundamental Rights.

furtherInformation:
The Code Success Fund focuses on:

1. Engaging civil society organizations, including community cultural centers, which work primarily at the local community level, in their capacity as strategic allies for embedding EU values in their communities and spreading the ideas of democracy, human rights, and the inclusion of vulnerable groups through the application of the "learning through experience" methodology.

3. It is expected that the initiatives supported by the Fund will be proposed by organizations from different regions of the country working with their communities.

results.summary: Call for proposals for small grants 3/SPLOT/GM/2026
results.content: Call for proposals for small grants 3/SPLOT/GM/2026

beneficiaryAdministration:
Link to the application platform: http://siecsplot.pl/splot-wartosci/

The value of the grant cannot be lower than EUR 2,500 or higher than EUR 7,500. No own contribution is required.

Objectives of the grant fund:

1.  strengthening the potential of civil society organisations and supported leaders to promote and protect EU values ​​and fundamental rights,

2.    strengthening the ability of supported organisations to represent the CSO sector and make effective decisions,

3.    increasing the presence of CSOs in public life and leaders in the forum of public debate,

4.    raising the level of involvement in law-making processes,

5.    strengthening the image of CSOs - a more favourable environment for civil society organisations,

6.    strengthening awareness of the importance of democratic values ​​for civil society and the role of organisations in their active promotion and protection.

The application is subject to a point assessment carried out by a team of experts gathered in the competition committee. Each application is assessed independently by 2 experts (experts sign an impartiality clause towards the assessed Grantee).

Subject criteria for grant projects

Grant projects submitted in the call must meet the following subject criteria:

Criterion 1 – The implementation of the grant project must relate to the priorities of the CERV programme - raising awareness of rights and values ​​by supporting civil society organisations; strengthening the protection and promotion of Union values, including respect for the rule of law; contributing to the implementation of democratic values, including by supporting dialogue, transparency and good governance, including in cases of shrinking space for civil society. Criterion verified on the basis of the Information contained in the application.

Criterion 2 - Implementation of the project exclusively in Poland. Fulfilment of this criterion is verified on the basis of the provisions in the application.

Criterion 3 – The value of the requested grant cannot be less than EUR 2,500 or more than EUR 7,500. Fulfilment of this criterion is verified on the basis of the provisions in the application.

Criterion 4 - Duration of the grant from 3 to 12 months. Grants in call no. 3/SPLOT/GM/2026 may be implemented in the period from March 1, 2027 to May 31, 2027. Fulfillment of this criterion is verified based on the application records.

Criterion 5 – Grant project settled using simplified methods based on results.

Criterion 6 – Project implemented by one entity.

Further information

Entities eligible to apply for a grant are independent civil society organisations registered in Poland, including organisations that:

1.    have their registered office in Poland,

2.    are non-profit (do not operate for profit),

3.    operate at local and/or regional and/or national level,

4.    respect fundamental rights and values ​​on which the EU is based,

5.    carry out activities in the areas covered by the CERV programme,

6.    are neither affiliated entities with the Grantor, nor have they been collaborators or contractors within 12 months prior to the date of application.
description:
The following activities of the Grantees may be financed under the grants:

- Raising awareness of the rights and values enshrined in the EU Treaties and the Charter and reaching out to the general public and key actors such as policymakers and legislators, legal practitioners and the judiciary; communication and information campaigns via social media.

- Organising citizens' platforms and citizens' dialogues on topics related to EU rights and values (including through the use of digital technologies).

- Coalitions and partnerships between civil society organisations; coordination and strategic cooperation between civil society organisations and other stakeholders, public or private sector actors.

- Providing free advice, supervision and monitoring of EU policies, rights and values as enshrined in the EU Treaties and the Charter.

- Promotion of the implementation of adopted laws, regulations and court cases.

- Citizen participation/lobbying/advocacy to influence policy and contribute to decision-making processes (at national, regional or local level), including review/update/adoption of policies and legislation.

- Research and analysis to inform policy-making at EU and national level, develop tools and standards to support EU values.

- Providing targeted support services such as victim support, psychological support to deal with online and offline threats, etc.

Only activities carried out in Poland are eligible. Grant projects can be local, regional or nationwide.

results.summary: Cultural Horizons: Innovative Cultural Products
results.content: Cultural Horizons: Innovative Cultural Products

beneficiaryAdministration:
The ‘Cultural Horizons’ programme is designed to increase the access of Ukrainians, particularly displaced persons, to culture and cultural heritage, by supporting cultural and artistic projects developed through EU-Ukrainian partnerships. It aims to strengthen connections between the Ukrainian and EU cultural spheres and to explore mentorship as a tool for professional development.


The ‘Cultural Horizons’ programme is co-financed by the EU through Creative Europe and implemented by the Ukrainian Cultural Foundation (Ukraine) with Cultural Vistas gGmbH (Germany).


The programme aims to:

1) Strengthen connections between the Ukrainian and EU cultural sectors;

2) Explore and promote mentorship as a tool for the development of the culture sector;  

3) Foster the professional development of Ukrainian artists and cultural actors. 


Within the programme, five open calls will be launched.


This is the first call - “Innovative cultural products” aims to support the development of various cultural sectors through the implementation of innovative approaches, including interdisciplinarity, the use of cutting-edge digital technologies (such as AR/VR, artificial intelligence, and big data), new formats of audience engagement, as well as flexible models of governance and cultural entrepreneurship.


Eligibility: partnerships between Ukrainian and EU-based organisations, individual entrepreneurs (with the Ukrainian partner acting as a lead applicant).


Total budget of the call: EUR 400 000 (UAH 19 108 000)

Minimum grant amount: EUR 10 000 (UAH 500 000)

Maximum grant amount: EUR 20 000 (UAH 1 000 000)


Please note that the total budget of the call in UAH may be increased or decreased depending on changes in the average monthly accounting exchange rates published by the European Commission through InforEuro and applied on the date of the decision to initiate the negotiation (grant agreement preparation) process for projects recommended for funding under this call.


Timeline


Technical eligibility check: 17–31 August 2026

Expert evaluation: until 12 November 2026

GA signature: by February 2027

 

Project implementation start: not earlier than 31 January 2027

Project implementation end: 30 July 2027 (incl. reporting).

results.summary: Culture Helps Solidarity - Fifth Call for Proposals for Individual Grants
results.content: Culture Helps Solidarity - Fifth Call for Proposals for Individual Grants

beneficiaryAdministration:
Culture Helps Solidarity - Open Call for Individual Grant

Fifth round, 25 August - 8 September 2026

Culture Helps Solidarity supports arts and culture professionals from Ukraine to sustain creativity, resilience, and community connection during and after the war. Running until 2028, the project combines three grant schemes - individual grants, thematic project grants, and collaboration grants - with a rich programme of mentoring, learning, and peer exchange. The project is co-funded through the Creative Europe programme and implemented by the European Cultural Foundation (Amsterdam), an independent foundation fostering European belonging through culture; together with Insha Osvita (Kyiv), a Ukrainian NGO and professional learning community developing educational and cultural programmes; zusa (Berlin), an international NGO fostering collaboration and collective learning for social and cultural change; and the VETERANKA Movement (Kyiv), Ukraine's leading community of women veterans advocating for women's rights, leadership, and reintegration.

The Individual Grants provide direct, flexible support to cultural professionals in and from Ukraine who are working - often voluntarily - with displaced people and refugees, veterans and vulnerable communities, in Ukraine or in any of the Creative Europe (CE) countries (which include the 27 EU member-states and more countries participating in Creative Europe).

These personal care grants are designed to offer quick and accessible assistance for strengthening the personal wellbeing, resilience and mental health of cultural professionals and creatives, enabling them to continue their crucial cultural, community-based work in extremely challenging circumstances. These grants are not designed to cover costs related to project delivery or implementation.

This is the fifth call in the series of rolling application rounds, opening approximately every six weeks. Across the 2026-2028 project period, we anticipate 10–14 such cycles. In each cycle, approximately 7 to 10 grants of up to EUR 1,200 will be disbursed.


WHO IS IT FOR?

This call seeks to support individual professionals in need for individual wellbeing care who work in arts, culture or community-based cultural activities and:

  1. support displaced Ukrainians, both inside Ukraine and across Creative Europe countries;
  2. play a meaningful and publicly relevant role for maintaining cultural production, artistic creation or community life in Ukraine or in Creative Europe countries;
  3. work with veterans and vulnerable groups;
  4. seek urgent personal wellbeing support that will enable them to continue their work, creative practice, and engagement with their communities;
  5. have been personally affected by war, displacement, and/or traumatic working conditions.


WHAT DO WE OFFER?

We offer up to €1,200 (including taxes if applicable) per individual, disbursed as a one-off contribution. The grant may be used strictly for personal mental health and wellbeing support and may not be directed to third parties, to project implementation or organisational costs.

Eligible activities include:

  1. Psychotherapy or psychological counselling;
  2. Trauma-informed coaching or emotional (group) support sessions;
  3. Restorative care or rehabilitation stays (e.g., sanatorium treatment, wellness programmes, retreats);
  4. Visit to cultural institutions and events (tickets to museums, theatres, cinemas, concerts, etc.); 
  5. Participation in master classes or workshops (art therapy) and materials for participation in them, if necessary; 
  6. Other justified wellbeing-oriented services that directly support the applicant’s resilience.

The grant may not be used for:

  1. psychiatric consultations or medical mental‑health treatment (including any expenses that involve medical care, diagnosis);
  2. purchase of medication or medical devices (even if prescribed by a doctor);
  3. purchase of material assets (tools, household items, equipment, etc., consumables for work, etc.);
  4. payment of rent for premises (residential or commercial, non-residential); 
  5. tuition fees, other training costs (formal or informal);
  6. invasive interventions (surgical operations, cosmetic procedures, dental interventions, etc.);
  7. streaming platform subscriptions;
  8. consultations with doctors of alternative medical practice;
  9. strictly humanitarian needs or cost-of-living support.


ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA:

Individual grants are strictly dedicated to individuals, who:

  1. are aged 18 and above;
  2.  reside in Ukraine or have fled from Ukraine to one of the Creative Europe countries (which include the 27 EU member states and more countries participating in Creative Europe);
  3. artists, cultural managers, or activists and volunteers working with displaced persons in Ukraine, or with displaced persons and refugees from Ukraine in one of the Creative Europe countries, veterans and vulnerable groups;
  4. submit a complete application form in either Ukrainian or English language.


SELECTION CRITERIA AND PROCESS:

  1. Relevance of professional context – Does the applicant demonstrate a convincing role within their artistic, cultural, or cultural-community environment, and clearly explain the relevance of their engagement through artistic practice, cultural production, and/or culture-based community initiatives?
  2. Personal wellbeing relevance – Is the requested support clearly related to maintaining or strengthening the applicant's personal wellbeing and resilience at this stage of their life and work?
  3. Public and community impact – Is the applicant able to convincingly demonstrate how sustaining their own wellbeing and resilience would support their continued contribution to arts, culture, and/or culture-based community life, generating benefits for the communities, audiences, or cultural environments with which they engage?
  4. Coherence and feasibility of the planned use of funds - Are the requested activities realistic and eligible to the purpose of supporting the applicant's wellbeing.

Following an eligibility check, applications will be assessed by external advisors who are familiar with the cultural sector and the current context in Ukraine. Final decisions will be made by the consortium partners, who review the recommendations to ensure consistency and budgetary balance. 7 to 10 applications will be awarded per round. 

TIMELINE: 


25 August 2026                                          fifth call for proposals open

27 August 2026                                           info session

8 September 2026                                      call closed

Beginning of October 2026                        proposals assessed and selected

12 October 2026                                        sixth call for proposals open


HOW TO APPLY?

The submission deadline for proposals is Tuesday, 8th of September 2026, 13:00 Amsterdam time/ 14:00 Kyiv time.

You can find more information and useful application tips, and complete the application form, including the budget section via this link: https://culture-of-solidarity-fund.grantplatform.com/ .

These personal care grants are designed to offer quick and accessible assistance for strengthening the personal wellbeing, resilience and mental health of cultural professionals and creatives, enabling them to continue their crucial cultural, community-based work in extremely challenging circumstances. These grants are not designed to cover costs related to project delivery or implementation.

This is the fifth call in the series of rolling application rounds, opening approximately every six weeks. Across the 2026-2028 project period, we anticipate 10–14 such cycles. In each cycle, approximately 7 to 10 grants of up to EUR 1,200 will be disbursed.


WHO IS IT FOR?

This call seeks to support individual professionals in need for individual wellbeing care who work in arts, culture or community-based cultural activities and:

  1. support displaced Ukrainians, both inside Ukraine and across Creative Europe countries;
  2. play a meaningful and publicly relevant role for maintaining cultural production, artistic creation or community life in Ukraine or in Creative Europe countries;
  3. work with veterans and vulnerable groups;
  4. seek urgent personal wellbeing support that will enable them to continue their work, creative practice, and engagement with their communities;
  5. have been personally affected by war, displacement, and/or traumatic working conditions.


WHAT DO WE OFFER?

We offer up to €1,200 (including taxes if applicable) per individual, disbursed as a one-off contribution. The grant may be used strictly for personal mental health and wellbeing support and may not be directed to third parties, to project implementation or organisational costs.

Eligible activities include:

  1. Psychotherapy or psychological counselling;
  2. Trauma-informed coaching or emotional (group) support sessions;
  3. Restorative care or rehabilitation stays (e.g., sanatorium treatment, wellness programmes, retreats);
  4. Visit to cultural institutions and events (tickets to museums, theatres, cinemas, concerts, etc.); 
  5. Participation in master classes or workshops (art therapy) and materials for participation in them, if necessary; 
  6. Other justified wellbeing-oriented services that directly support the applicant’s resilience.

The grant may not be used for:

  1. psychiatric consultations or medical mental‑health treatment (including any expenses that involve medical care, diagnosis);
  2. purchase of medication or medical devices (even if prescribed by a doctor);
  3. purchase of material assets (tools, household items, equipment, etc., consumables for work, etc.);
  4. payment of rent for premises (residential or commercial, non-residential); 
  5. tuition fees, other training costs (formal or informal);
  6. invasive interventions (surgical operations, cosmetic procedures, dental interventions, etc.);
  7. streaming platform subscriptions;
  8. consultations with doctors of alternative medical practice;
  9. strictly humanitarian needs or cost-of-living support.


ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA:

Individual grants are strictly dedicated to individuals, who:

  1. are aged 18 and above;
  2.  reside in Ukraine or have fled from Ukraine to one of the Creative Europe countries (which include the 27 EU member states and more countries participating in Creative Europe);
  3. artists, cultural managers, or activists and volunteers working with displaced persons in Ukraine, or with displaced persons and refugees from Ukraine in one of the Creative Europe countries, veterans and vulnerable groups;
  4. submit a complete application form in either Ukrainian or English language.


SELECTION CRITERIA AND PROCESS:

  1. Relevance of professional context – Does the applicant demonstrate a convincing role within their artistic, cultural, or cultural-community environment, and clearly explain the relevance of their engagement through artistic practice, cultural production, and/or culture-based community initiatives?
  2. Personal wellbeing relevance – Is the requested support clearly related to maintaining or strengthening the applicant's personal wellbeing and resilience at this stage of their life and work?
  3. Public and community impact – Is the applicant able to convincingly demonstrate how sustaining their own wellbeing and resilience would support their continued contribution to arts, culture, and/or culture-based community life, generating benefits for the communities, audiences, or cultural environments with which they engage?
  4. Coherence and feasibility of the planned use of funds - Are the requested activities realistic and eligible to the purpose of supporting the applicant's wellbeing.

Following an eligibility check, applications will be assessed by external advisors who are familiar with the cultural sector and the current context in Ukraine. Final decisions will be made by the consortium partners, who review the recommendations to ensure consistency and budgetary balance. 7 to 10 applications will be awarded per round. 

TIMELINE: 


25 August 2026                                          fifth call for proposals open

27 August 2026                                           info session

8 September 2026                                      call closed

Beginning of October 2026                        proposals assessed and selected

12 October 2026                                        sixth call for proposals open


HOW TO APPLY?

The submission deadline for proposals is Tuesday, 8th of September 2026, 13:00 Amsterdam time/ 14:00 Kyiv time.

You can find more information and useful application tips, and complete the application form, including the budget section via this link: https://culture-of-solidarity-fund.grantplatform.com/ .

beneficiaryAdministration:
Culture Helps Solidarity - Open Call for Project Grants

Memory in Action

Support for projects in the fields of (tactical) commemoration, historical and artistic documentation, social and non-institutional archives as cultural heritage

Second Round, August-October, 2026


Culture Helps Solidarity supports arts and culture professionals from Ukraine to sustain creativity, resilience, and community connection during and after the war. Running until 2028, the project combines three grant schemes - individual grants, thematic project grants, and collaboration grants - with a rich programme of mentoring, learning, and peer exchange. The project is co-funded through the Creative Europe programme and implemented by the European Cultural Foundation (Amsterdam), an independent foundation fostering European belonging through culture, together with Insha Osvita (Kyiv), a Ukrainian NGO and professional learning community developing educational and cultural programmes; zusa (Berlin), an international NGO fostering collaboration and collective learning for social and cultural change; and the VETERANKA Movement (Kyiv), Ukraine's leading community of women veterans advocating for women's rights, leadership, and reintegration.

At least 60 Project Grants will be awarded across four thematic calls, with a minimum of 15 projects supported in this second round. Each project may receive up to €7,000. More information about the upcoming themes can be found at the end of this call for proposals.

Introduction & Thematic focus 

The second call for Projects Grants of Culture Helps Solidarity focuses on memory and commemoration projects that work responsibly with the lived experiences of people affected by Russia’s war against Ukraine. The call will support cultural and community-based initiatives that create meaningful forms of remembrance, documentation (both analog and digital), public reflection, and commemoration while respecting the dignity, safety, and agency of those whose stories and losses are represented. 

We are especially interested in projects that engage with the experiences and stories of women veterans, servicewomen, all veterans, families of the fallen, witnesses of wartime events, local residents, people who have experienced loss, captivity, injury, displacement and others directly connected to places, events, or histories of war.  

This call approaches commemoration not as a formal gesture, but as an ethical and community-centered practice. Supported projects should be attentive to trauma-informed principles, informed consent, privacy, emotional safety, and the responsible use of personal materials such as photographs, letters, messages, oral testimonies, family archives, objects, and memories both in analogue and digital formats. Applicants are encouraged to think carefully about how stories are told and represented, whose perspectives are centered, how people are invited into the process, what should remain private, and how to avoid extractive or harmful forms of representation. 

What are we looking for? 

This call supports small-scale cultural projects that engage with the experiences, memories, and histories of people directly affected by Russia’s war against Ukraine, including but not limited to women veterans, families of the fallen, displaced communities, local residents, people who have experienced loss, captivity, injury, or displacement, and witnesses of wartime events. We invite cultural workers, artists, researchers, community organisers, memory practitioners, and civil society initiatives based in Ukraine and across Europe to develop projects that approach remembrance as a careful, inclusive, and community-led practice. Through artistic, educational, research-based, or participatory formats, projects should create meaningful opportunities for reflection, strengthen local and collective memory across generations, amplify diverse voices, and help people feel seen and heard. Ultimately, the call seeks to support cultural practices that contribute to a more responsible public conversation about the ongoing impact and aftermath of Russia’s war against Ukraine, both within Ukraine and across Europe. 

We prioritise cultural projects that work with people and communities whose experiences, memories, and histories have been shaped by Russia’s war against Ukraine, including: 

  1. women veterans, servicewomen, and all veterans; 
  2. families of the fallen and those living with loss; 
  3. people who experienced captivity (civilians and military) including those who experienced illegal imprisonment in occupied territories; 
  4. displaced communities and people affected by forced relocation; 
  5. witnesses of wartime events; 
  6. other individuals and groups connected to places, events, landscapes or histories of war. 

Projects may take many cultural forms, such as co-creation processes, participatory or collaborative art, community storytelling and archiving, exhibitions, audio or visual storytelling, artistic documentation, community gatherings, local acts of remembrance, publications, educational art formats, and other cultural practices that help people process loss, preserve memory, and speak about the war with care.  

What matters above all is that activities approach remembrance as an ethical, inclusive, and community-centered practice. Projects should create meaningful opportunities for Ukrainians and all Europeans to reflect on and share experiences connected to Russia's war on Ukraine, while demonstrating sensitivity to trauma, informed consent, privacy, and emotional wellbeing. We are also interested in initiatives that strengthen collective memory among Ukrainians and all Europeans, amplify diverse voices, and contribute to more thoughtful and responsible conversations about the ongoing impact of war. 

What do we offer? 

We offer project grants of up to €7,000.   

The Project Grants can cover a large variety of costs including production costs, marketing and advertising costs, rental and running costs for studios and cultural venues, IT, communication and production tools and materials, and - upon special request and where appropriate (e.g. when lost/destroyed) - purchase of other goods, means, or services necessary for the implementation and execution of the project.  

Grants can also be used to cover travel costs, expert fees, artists' honoraria, legal services, staff - and operational costs. However, these amounts must all be proportionate and justifiable.  

Although co-financing is not mandatory, it is recommended that the grant is used to cover a maximum of 80% of the total project budget. 

The project timeline may be up to 6 months. Activities related to the project may not take place before the start date (1 February 2027). 

The submission deadline for proposals is Tuesday, 6 October 2026, 13:00 Amsterdam time/ 14:00 Kyiv time. 

 

Deepen Your Understanding – Watch the Webinar 

(Tactical) Commemoration/Artistic documentation; Social/heritage archive 

A webinar related to the thematic focus of this call was held on 23 June 2026. If you were unable to attend, you can now watch the recording and access the materials to gain a deeper understanding of key topics such as: 

  1. Key Principles of Trauma-Informed and Ethical Interaction When Collecting Testimonies and Personal Stories, by Larysa Denysenko;  
  2. Case study of the project “Skulpturnyi”: Artistic Engagement with Vulnerable Groups, by Marta Syrko;  
  3. Case study: Contemporary Approaches to Memory Projects and Engagement with Communities Directly Connected to This Memory, by Kateryna Semeniuk; 
  4. Specific Aspects of Cultural Projects for, about and with Women and Men Veterans, by Kateryna Demerza. 

 

Link to watch: https://youtu.be/fZIoSIzIkAQ?si=r3NWI5_R-MRcs7Z5  

 

Eligibility Criteria 

  1. Applications must be submitted in English or Ukrainian and must include a complete application form and budget; 
  2. Applicants must be above 18 years old; 
  3. This call is open to and civic, public or private1 organisations based in Ukraine or in any of the Creative Europe countries (which include the 27 EU member states and more countries participating in Creative Europe) and operate in the cultural, creative, or civil sector; 
  4. We welcome individuals with strong project ideas to apply. However, in order to smoothly navigate the administrative requirements of Creative Europe and the local tax authorities and to facilitate a prompt start of your project, we strongly recommend individual applicants to apply with an eligible civic, public or private organisation that can serve as their legal entity for concluding grant agreements; 
  5. The proposed project must not receive funding from any other Creative Europe scheme; 
  6. Proposals submitted by political parties will not be considered; 
  7. Strictly humanitarian initiatives or individual requests for cost-of living support will not be considered.  

Selection Criteria and Process 

  1. Relevance to the thematic focus - Does the project engage with the experiences and memories of people directly affected by war through cultural, artistic, educational, or participatory practices? Does it contribute to meaningful and inclusive forms of remembrance in Ukraine and across the rest of Europe? Does it amplify the voices of people and communities connected to places, events, or histories of war, and strengthen collective memory? Does it demonstrate a thoughtful, ethical, and community-centered approach, including sensitivity to trauma, informed consent, privacy, and the responsible representation of personal experiences and materials? 
  2. Capacity and competence of the applicant - Does the applicant demonstrate relevant experience, expertise, and motivation to work with communities affected by war and remembrance processes? Does the applicant show an understanding of ethical and trauma-informed approaches, including informed consent, privacy, and the responsible use of personal stories and materials? Is the team composition (if applicable) appropriate to deliver the proposed activities in a safe, respectful, and meaningful way? 
  3. Quality and coherence of the proposal - Are the aims, methods, and results well-articulated and realistic? Does the proposal demonstrate understanding of the communities involved, the sensitivities associated with memory, loss, and wartime experiences? Are the proposed methods appropriate to the project’s aims and grounded in ethical and community-centred practice? Is the timeline feasible and the budget justified? 
  4. Authenticity and experimentation - Does the project offer a thoughtful approach to remembrance, memory work, or artistic documentation? Does it use creative, participatory, or community-led methods to engage with experiences of war in meaningful and respectful ways? Does it demonstrate care in how stories, testimonies, and memories are collected, shared, or preserved? 
  5. Sustainability of action - Does the project show potential for continued impact beyond the grant period? Is there consideration of environmental responsibility?  

Following an eligibility check, proposals will be assessed by a team of internal and external experts from a wide range of geographic, cultural and professional areas. At least fifteen projects will be selected for support in this round. 

Timeline 

18 August 2026             call for proposals open 

6 October 2026             call closed 

End November – 

Beginning of December 2026     proposals assessed and selected  

1 February 2027 earliest starting date of selected projects 

31 July 2027              end date of selected projects 

31 August 2027              submission deadline for final reports 

 

Projects may not begin before 1 February 2027. 

How to Apply? 

You can find more information - including the budget template - and submit your application via this link: https://culture-of-solidarity-fund.grantplatform.com/ 




1 Private organisations must have a non-commercial status and must be able to prove the project’s charitable status.

https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/qLwzxAw8RO6tSbMMY-U1eg

Applicants are encouraged to develop their proposals through human expertise, critical thinking, and artistic or professional judgment. Proposals that rely primarily on AI-generated content or concepts may be given lower priority in the assessment process.

Should you have further questions, please contact us at chs@culturalfoundation.eu.

Culture Helps Solidarity / Культура допомагає: Солідарність is co-financed by the EU Creative Europe Programme and implemented by the European Cultural Foundation (NL), Insha Osvita (UA), zusa (DE), and the VETERANKA Movement (UA). 


Looking Ahead: Future Opportunities 

As you consider this call, here is a glimpse of what’s next. Over the course of the Culture Helps Solidarity programme, we will launch two additional thematic calls, each paired with a webinar to deepen your practice and connect you with peers across Ukraine and Europe. Please keep an eye on the upcoming announcements that may (better) resonate with your experience, your community, or your artistic approach. 

Call & Webinar No. 3: Community Spaces as Safer Environments — January 2027 In this round we will examine how community spaces serve as anchor points for people in displacement. The focus is on creating environments where belonging is nurtured and integration becomes a shared responsibility between newcomers and local residents. 

  1. Key themes: Defining "safer spaces" intergenerational resilience, guidelines for working with people with combat experience, and destigmatizing mental health through open conversation. 

Call & Webinar No. 4: Ecologies of Care — May 2027 The final call addresses the ecological rupture caused by war. We invite cultural initiatives to respond to the destruction of Ukraine’s ecosystems not only as a human tragedy but as an opportunity to reimagine our interdependence with the "more-than-human" world. 

  1. Key themes: Living with damaged landscapes, ancestral knowledge, and regenerative futures.

beneficiaryAdministration:
The ‘Cultural Horizons’ programme is designed to increase the access of Ukrainians, particularly displaced persons, to culture and cultural heritage, by supporting cultural and artistic projects developed through EU-Ukrainian partnerships. It aims to strengthen connections between the Ukrainian and EU cultural spheres and to explore mentorship as a tool for professional development.

The ‘Cultural Horizons’ programme is co-financed by the EU through Creative Europe and implemented by the Ukrainian Cultural Foundation (Ukraine) with Cultural Vistas gGmbH (Germany).

The programme aims to:

1) Strengthen connections between the Ukrainian and EU cultural sectors;

2) Explore and promote mentorship as a tool for the development of the culture sector;  

3) Foster the professional development of Ukrainian artists and cultural actors. 

The 'Artistic Debuts' call seeks to help graduates of arts education institutions establish themselves as artists and cultural professionals, develop their creative potential, and build sustainable cooperation with cultural institutions. The call also supports educational institutions that provide training in the fields of culture and the arts—including arts universities and academies, universities of culture and the arts, and other higher education institutions offering relevant study programmes—as well as providers of non-formal arts education, such as creative studios, art schools and workshops, and cultural and educational centres. By strengthening collaboration between emerging artists and educational and cultural institutions, the call contributes to creating favourable conditions for the professional development of early-career artists and their successful integration into Ukraine’s cultural sector.

Eligibility: partnerships between Ukrainian and EU-based organisations, individual entrepreneurs (with the Ukrainian partner acting as a lead applicant), legal entities and individual entrepreneurs based in Ukraine


Total budget of the Call: 350 000 € (UAH 18 000 000)

Minimum grant amount: 5 000 € (UAH 250 000)

Maximum grant amount: 14 000 € (UAH 715 000)


Please note that the total budget of the call in UAH may be increased or decreased depending on changes in the average monthly accounting exchange rates published by the European Commission through InforEuro and applied on the date of the decision to initiate the negotiation (grant agreement preparation) process for projects recommended for funding under this call.


Timeline

Technical eligibility check: until 19.10.2026

Expert evaluation: until 26.11.2026

GA signature: until 15.03.2027


Project implementation start: not earlier than 15 March 2027

Project implementation end: 15 August 2027 (incl. reporting).

duration: Implementation of funded projects - up to 5 months
destinationDetails:
The ‘Cultural Horizons’ programme is designed to increase the access of Ukrainians, particularly displaced persons, to culture and cultural heritage, by supporting cultural and artistic projects developed through EU-Ukrainian partnerships. It aims to strengthen connections between the Ukrainian and EU cultural spheres and to explore mentorship as a tool for professional development.

The ‘Cultural Horizons’ programme is co-financed by the EU through Creative Europe and implemented by the Ukrainian Cultural Foundation (Ukraine) with Cultural Vistas gGmbH (Germany).

The programme aims to:

1) Strengthen connections between the Ukrainian and EU cultural sectors;

2) Explore and promote mentorship as a tool for the development of the culture sector;  

3) Foster the professional development of Ukrainian artists and cultural actors. 

The 'Artistic Debuts' call seeks to help graduates of arts education institutions establish themselves as artists and cultural professionals, develop their creative potential, and build sustainable cooperation with cultural institutions. The call also supports educational institutions that provide training in the fields of culture and the arts—including arts universities and academies, universities of culture and the arts, and other higher education institutions offering relevant study programmes—as well as providers of non-formal arts education, such as creative studios, art schools and workshops, and cultural and educational centres. By strengthening collaboration between emerging artists and educational and cultural institutions, the call contributes to creating favourable conditions for the professional development of early-career artists and their successful integration into Ukraine’s cultural sector.

Eligibility: partnerships between Ukrainian and EU-based organisations, individual entrepreneurs (with the Ukrainian partner acting as a lead applicant), legal entities and individual entrepreneurs based in Ukraine


Total budget of the Call: 350 000 € (UAH 18 000 000)

Minimum grant amount: 5 000 € (UAH 250 000)

Maximum grant amount: 14 000 € (UAH 715 000)


Please note that the total budget of the call in UAH may be increased or decreased depending on changes in the average monthly accounting exchange rates published by the European Commission through InforEuro and applied on the date of the decision to initiate the negotiation (grant agreement preparation) process for projects recommended for funding under this call.


Timeline

Technical eligibility check: until 19.10.2026

Expert evaluation: until 26.11.2026

GA signature: until 15.03.2027


Project implementation start: not earlier than 15 March 2027

Project implementation end: 15 August 2027 (incl. reporting).

results.content: DIGITWIN4CIUE project-Scholarships for the Executive Master in Digital Twins on Infrastructures and Cities

beneficiaryAdministration:
Purpose

DIGITWIN4CIUE is a project aligned with the Digital programme, and the project aimed to retain and attract to the EU the best talents worldwide. Therefore, it is soliciting applications for scholarships dedicated only for facilitating the physical mobility to follow the courses with physical attendance to the three on-site events organized during the course. The intention of this scholarship is to benefit students from the project's high-quality education in digital areas and promote equality in the field of digital twins for infrastructures and cities. Everyone is welcome to apply regardless of their personal situation, but gender equality and socioeconomic status are also factors to receiving this scholarship.

The scholarship is destined to promote mobility of the students in the master and are offered in the form of a discount in the fee. The scholarships for the eligible students of the master program have a fixed amount of EUR 2,000 per student. This amount shall be used by the students of the master (or the sponsoring entities) to partially cover the traveling and accommodation costs of the students to attend to the onsite events of the master program.


Applications

Those interested must read the requirements below and fill in the online form available on the BME-e-platform Course: Digital Twins for Complex Infrastructures and Urban Ecosystems 2025 (bme.hu)

Candidates will be required to complete four forms to evaluate their background. Among other information, candidates will be required to upload the following documentation:

  1. Accredited degree certificate (Diploma) or proof of having applied for certificate. Additionally, graduates from an University outside the European Higher Education Area (EHEA, click here to see the members of the EHEA), are required to submit duly legalized university degree certificate before December of the academic year. This certificate can be obtained as follows:
  2. By means of the Hague Convention Apostille if the graduate comes from signatory countries of the Apostille of the Hague (click here for the signatory countries). In this case, the authorities of the certificate-issuing country accredit that it is a valid degree certificate and has been issued by the competent authority.
  3. By a legal stamp of the Embassies and Consulates of Spain in the country of issue, for graduates from non-signatory countries of the Apostille of the Hague. In this case, the diploma and records can be legalized by the stamp of the Embassies and Consulates of Spain in the country of issue of your diploma that certifies it is an official university degree. For more information look at the question “Legalization of foreign documents abroad via diplomatic channels” in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' web (click here to enter the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' web).
  4. Transcript of university academic records and diplomas, translated to English, French or Spanish.
  5. Proof of English language skills (TOEFL, IELTS or similar, taken in the last 2 years), or alternatively a written statement proving that the candidate meets the required English level. The language skills may be evaluated lately in a personal interview with candidates. and a personal interview.
  6. Curriculum Vitae in English.
  7. Copy of official identification (national ID or passport)
  8. A short video in English of 3 minutes max, summarizing your interest in the master. Alternatively, a document summarizing your motivation to participate in the master program.


Principal requirements for applicants

The scholarship will only be granted to individuals or entities that do not fall under the list of entities subject to EU restrictive measures under Article 29 of the Treaty on the European Union (TEU) and Article 215 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (TFEU)14 and entities covered by Commission Guidelines No 2013/C 205/05, and that have already been admitted (or are sponsoring an admitted candidate) to the Executive Master in Digital Twins for Infrastructures and cities master's program. This means that to be considered for the scholarship applicants will meet the following requirements:

1.Have applied to the master through the Apply section Digital Twins for Complex Infrastructures and Urban Ecosystems - Digital Twins - Infrastructures & CIties (digitwin4ciue.eu) and:

  1. Have the availability to attend to the online live sessions and to the three workshops that will be held in November, February and June/July.
  2. Hold a bachelor’s degree of at least 240 ECTS issued by a recognized University in the field of Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Engineering, or Architecture, or any similar technical degree. Alternatively, candidates holding a bachelor’s degree of 180 ECTS of similar nature will be eligible with a previous working experience of at least 2 years in any field of the built environment.
  3. Previous working experience is not required (save for candidates holding a BSc of 180 ECTS) but will be valued for the acceptance committee. A minimum of 3 years’ experience is preferred.
  4. Have English language skills equivalent to a minimum of IELTS 6.5 with 5.5 in each subtest, or TOEFL 80 or any other test or evidence to accredit an English level of at least B2
  5. Should have basic skills in any programming language. Otherwise, they will be required to attend to free programming courses before the start of the master.
  6. Be national of an elegible country, including.
  7. Listed EEA countries and countries associated with the Digital Euroepe Programme by 2021.
  8. Accept that the net amount of the tuition fee includes the EUR2,000 scholarship as a discount.


Selection criteria

Academic merit will be the predominant factor in deciding who gets the scholarship. In case of receiving more than 200 applications per year, the committee has agreed a set of guidelines with the configured on the following main eligibility criteria.

  1. Contribute to promoting diversity in terms of gender, age and geographical distribution.
  2. Contribute to promoting the access to the master of students of lower income.
  3. Contribute to promoting the training of professionals of SMEs and entrepreneurs.


Payment arrangements

The scholarship is reflected as a discount in the tuition fee. The candidates are informed of the net amount of the tuition fee, after deducting the applicable amount of the scholarship. The webpage clearly indicates that the tuition fees are inclusive of a scholarship of EUR2,000 which is co-funded by the EU Digital Europe Programme, under the project DIGITWIN4CIUE.


Budget

  1. The budget for edition 2025-26 is EUR 400.000€, with a maximum amount per scholarship of EUR 2,000.


Scholarship Compatibility Policy

The DIGITWIN4CIUE project-Scholarships for the Executive Master in Digital Twins on Infrastructures and Cities are compatible with any other DIGITWIN4CIUE project scholarships. These scholarships are co-financed (50%) by the European Union.

However, other scholarships are not compatible if their combined total exceeds the full cost of the master’s program, nor may they be used for any purpose other than the one originally intended. 

Additionally, the scholarships offered in this call are not compatible with other tuition fee scholarships, unless explicitly stated otherwise in the call for the other scholarship.

results.summary: RTU MERIT Project Mobility Scholarship September, 2026
results.content: RTU MERIT Project Mobility Scholarship September, 2026

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. The aim of the Mobility Scholarships (hereinafter referred to as SCHOLARSHIPS) is to support students who achieve excellent academic results and first and second-year students completing the full curriculum to extend their knowledge and skills in Cybersecurity (one of the MERIT target areas) for students without an ICT background.
  2. The SCHOLARSHIPS are granted by the MERIT project. MERIT project is co-funded by the European Union under grant agreement No. 101083531. Up to 50,000 euros are available to be distributed for the targeted scholarships at Riga Technical University (hereinafter referred to as RTU). 
  3. The SCHOLARSHIPS can be awarded to persons (hereinafter referred to as APPLICANTS) who are citizens of the European Union (hereinafter referred to as the EU) studying in the MERIT project master's degree program “Management of Smart, Resilient, and Interconnected Systems” (MERIT) (hereinafter referred to as the PROGRAM) at RTU. 
  4. If the number of eligible applications exceeds the available funding or the planned number of scholarships, applications will first be ranked based on academic merit. In cases of equal merit (ex aequo), preference may be given to promote diversity, including students with a non-ICT background and students from low DESI-index countries (i.e. countries below the EU average in at least basic digital skills, DESI 2025 (data from 2023)). This diversity-related criterion shall be applied only as a tie-break mechanism and shall not affect the equal treatment of applications. 
  5. Information about the scholarship is published on the RTU’s website (ttps://rbs.lv/merit/) - MERIT Mobility Scholarship. 
  6. Procedures for awarding SCHOLARSHIPS. 
  7. A student who has been matriculated to the MERIT curriculum of master's studies has the right to apply for the MERIT scholarship within the academic year, in September, starting from the first semester of the academic year of his/her matriculation, and if he/she 
  8.  is a full-time student; 
  9.  has completed the curriculum cumulatively in full. The study volume to be completed per semester is 30 ECTS; 
  10. has not exceeded the standard duration of the curriculum; 
  11. is not on academic leave; 
  12. To apply for the MERIT scholarship, the student submits an application form https://forms.gle/2CgdQNPsRsw5xNkx7 by 31 August 2026. The application must indicate: student identification number (Student’s ID), student's first and last name, and the bank account number of the scholarship recipient. 
  13. If the student has been studying at a foreign educational institution during the last semester mentioned above, the study merits have to be provided for the last semester of study at the university according to existing regulations and practices of the university issuing the merits document. 
  14. The outcome of the call for awarding the MERIT scholarship is published on RTU’s website. 
  15. The amount of the MERIT scholarship is eight hundred, and fifty euros (850) per student for a single mobility action, which will take place starting from 29th of September, 2026 until the 30th of September, 2026 at MERIT partner VILNIUS TECH (Vilnius Gediminas Technical University, Lithuania Homepage - VILNIUS TECH)
  16. The recipients of the MERIT scholarship shall be confirmed by the director of RBS no later than five working days before the date of payment of the scholarship in accordance with clause 6.2. The MERIT scholarship shall be transferred to the recipient's bank account on the basis of the order of the director. 
  17. The MERIT scholarship is paid no later than 1 week before the mobility action, i.e. 22th of September, 2026. 
  18. If the recipient of the MERIT scholarship is ex-matriculated (except when completing the curriculum) or goes on academic leave before the date of payment of the scholarship, the scholarship will not be paid to him or her.  
  19. The received money can be used for direct costs of the mobility, which include: 
  20. Transportation to and from the venue; 
  21. Per Diem expenses; 
  22. Accommodations; 
  23. Traveling insurance; 
  24. Local transportation to and from the venue; 
  25. All students receiving the scholarship are obliged to submit self-assessment report on acquired knowledge, skills and mobility experience (according to the template prepared by study program director).  

 

Legal disclaimer: 

This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by Riga Technical University (RTU). The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by RTU in its own name and under its own responsibility. RTU’s own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants who will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim of increasing the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of RTU.

  1. Read carefully the requirements and criteria published in Master in Digital Twins - Digital Twins - Infrastructures & Cities

  8. Proof of payment of the reservation fee

  1. Have applied to the master through the Apply section Digital Twins for Complex Infrastructures and Urban Ecosystems - Digital Twins - Infrastructures & CIties (digitwin4ciue.eu).

  7. Commit to successfully completing all 60 ECTS credits during the first academic year of enrolment.

beneficiaryAdministration:
1.  Aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships 

The aim of the Triple Degree Scholarships (hereinafter referred to as SCHOLARSHIPS) is to support students to complete their full curriculum with a triple degree programme at the University of Pavia and Grenoble School of Management to extend their knowledge and skills in advanced digital technologies (one of the DIGI-ME target areas).

2.     DIGI-ME Scholarships 

The SCHOLARSHIPS are granted by the DIGI-ME project. The DIGI-ME project is co-funded by the European Union under grant agreement No. 101123009. Up to 90,000 euros are available to be distributed for the targeted scholarships at the University of Vaasa. Through this call, up to 10 (ten) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their economic participation into the DIGI-ME path of the triple degree programme with the University of Pavia and with Grenoble School of Management. 

3.     Financial value

3.1 Scholarships are provided as a lump sum to cover living and subsistence costs. Each selected beneficiary will receive a lump sum for a single mobility action of 8 to 10 months, depending on the individual Learning Agreement, in the period from January 2027 until May 2027 at the University of Pavia (Italy) and in the period from August 2027 until December 2027 at Grenoble School of Management (France). The scholarship comprises a minimum of two components (items A and B) and a maximum of three components (items A, B, and C).


3.1.1 Fix components:


ITEM A: Monthly contribution: € 500,00;

ITEM B: Travel contribution per destination: € 700,00 (one-time fee);


3.1.2 Additional component based on special conditions: 


ITEM C: Monthly contribution for participants with fewer opportunities: €250,00;

Participants with fewer opportunities are defined as students who, prior to the start of the mobility period, meet one or more of the following criteria:

  1. have a disability with a certified percentage of invalidity of at least 50%; 

2.     hold refugee status and/or benefit from international or subsidiary protection, or are displaced persons; 

3.     have dependent minor children (Students who have given birth to a child during the 2026/27 academic year, as proven by the birth certificate, up to the child's first birthday);

4.     are engaged in employment (Students employed, other than occasionally and not employed by a family member up to and including the second degree, for a period of no less than six months within the 12 months preceding the mobility period, in any documented employment, self-employment, or professional activity, in the public or private sector);

5.     are recognised professional athletes (Students who are athletes of national interest must present a certificate from their relevant sports federation);

6.     are orphans of at least one parent (A student is considered to be an orphan of at least one parent if their father and/or mother have died before the date of submission of the mobility application. This status is recognized provided that the student: (a) has not turned 26 years old at the date of submission of the application, and/or (b) was financially dependent on the deceased parent at the time of death, or is in a similarly economically dependent situation);

7.     are children of victims of terrorism or organised crime. 

Supporting documents for item C will be requested only from successful applicants.

4.     Payment mechanism

4.1 The DIGI-ME scholarship is paid in two instalments:

4.1.1 First tranche equal to 80% of the total estimated amount of the scholarship, and paid within 30 days of signing the Mobility Agreement, provided that the student: 

1.     has presented a Learning Agreement duly approved and signed by the University of Vaasa and the host Higher Educational Institution;

2.     has correctly entered the bank details in the Reserved Area.

In the absence of even one of the conditions indicated above, the payment of the first tranche will be made within 30 days of their actual satisfaction.

4.1.2 Second tranche with a balance of 20%, paid at the end of the mobility, subject to verification of compliance with the following conditions: fulfilment of the administrative and procedural obligations set out in this call;

1.     regular completion of the authorised mobility period;

2.     achievement of training results consistent with the Learning Agreement;

3.     correct administrative conclusion of the mobility.

Failure to comply with even one of the above conditions will result in the loss of the right to the balance payment and may lead to the total or partial recovery of the sums already received.

Acceptance of the mobility period constitutes a formal commitment by the candidate. Cancellations must therefore be limited to serious and duly documented cases of force majeure. Any cancellation of the assigned mobility period must be communicated in writing to the DIGI-ME coordinator, digi-me@unipv.it, must be adequately justified, and must be submitted promptly. Cancellation entails the refund of any financial contributions already received. The reason for the cancellation and/or failure to communicate it may be evaluated for the purposes of possible exclusion of the candidate from the subsequent selection process for the University's international mobility programs.


4.2 Tax treatment

4.2.1 The scholarship provided under this call is subject to the applicable Finnish tax legislation. Depending on the nature and purpose of the grant, it may be either tax-exempt or taxable income and may need to be declared in the recipient’s tax return.

4.2.2 Grants or scholarships awarded for studies, academic research, or artistic activities may be tax-exempt. If the grant is paid by a public authority (e.g. the State of Finland, a municipality, or other public bodies), it is generally fully tax-exempt regardless of the amount. If the grant is paid by a private entity, it is tax-exempt only up to the annual limit defined by the State artist grant; any amount exceeding this threshold may be considered taxable income.

4.2.3 Grants are subject to certain mandatory contributions, including the health insurance contribution and the public broadcasting tax. In addition, grant recipients are typically covered by pension insurance under the MYEL system, and the corresponding income may be taken into account when calculating social security contributions.

4.2.4 It should be noted that tax exemption applies only to grants awarded for studies, academic research, or artistic activity. Grants awarded for other purposes are generally considered taxable earned income, regardless of the payer. Recipients are responsible for verifying their individual tax situation and complying with all applicable tax obligations. For more information, please refer to Grants - vero.fi .

5.     Evaluation process  

Submission will be done EXCLUSIVELY via the following dedicated form by 15 October 2026. A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes (which will be also shared with the European Commission). Applications that pass the eligibility check will undergo an internal evaluation, conducted by a panel of experts from the University of Vaasa. For more information on the selection and evaluation process please refer to the Guidelines for Applications. The outcome of the call for awarding the DIGI-ME scholarship will be published on the University of Vaasa DIGI-ME project’s website. 

6.     Eligibility criteria

The following persons are eligible for scholarships: 

6.1 Students regularly enrolled [1]in the DIGI-ME project master's degree programmes “Master’s Programme in International Business – Sustainable Global Business (MIB)” and “Master’s Programme in Strategic Business Development (SBD)” at the University of Vaasa:

1. matriculated in the academic year 2026-2027; 

2. full-time students;

3. who have not exceeded the standard duration of the curriculum;

4. not on academic leave.

6.2 Citizens of the European Union (hereinafter referred to as the EU) or DEP Countries (the full list is available here: list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf )

6.3 Proficiency in English is a fundamental requirement, as it is the official language of both the Open Call and the master's programmes. Unless the applicant is a native English speaker, they must provide a certified score report meeting minimum thresholds: an IELTS Academic score of 6.5, a TOEFL iBT score of 88, or a Cambridge English (C1/C2) score of 180; or having successfully completed a fully-English taught bachelor degree.

6.4 The scholarship covered by this call is INCOMPATIBLE with other EU funds allocated for the same purpose. All applicants must declare they have not received other European Union’s funds in the dedicated form. 

7.     Required Documents 


7.1 Transcripts of Records: Official transcript of records showing grades from the most recently completed studies. If the student has completed studies at a foreign educational institution during the academic year 2025–2026, an official transcript of those study achievements must also be provided in accordance with the regulations and practices of the issuing institution.

7.2 Curriculum Vitae (CV): A detailed CV outlining academic history, professional experience, skills, and relevant achievements (no photo required, max 3 pages).

7.3 Personal Statement/Motivation Letter/Study Plan: A statement (max. 700 words) explaining motivation for applying, interest in the programme, and how applicant’s background aligns with the DIGI-ME path of the triple degree programme at the University of Pavia and Grenoble School of Management. 

7.4 English Language Competency: Certified evidence of English proficiency meeting the specified minimum scores above. 

7.5 Copy of passport or ID card: Copy of a valid passport or identity card.

7.6 Optional: Information on gender, age, and socio-economic status. In case of equal scores, these factors may be positively considered during evaluation, in line with the University of Vaasa commitment to supporting a diverse student body.


8.     Evaluation Criteria and Scoring


8.1 Only eligible candidates will be evaluated. Successful candidates must reach an evaluation threshold of 70%. 

8.2 Applications are assessed based on three components:

  1. Academic background (65%) is assessed based on the weighted average grade, adjusted by the ratio of earned to expected ECTS credits. 

2.     Motivation (25%) reflects applicant’s positive mindset towards advanced digital skills in innovation, international business and entrepreneurship assessed based on the motivation letter.

3.     Additional experience (10%) considers both academic and non-academic achievements as reported in the applicant’s CV.

8.3. DIGI-ME and the University of Vaasa are committed to promoting diversity, social and economic equality, and gender balance in all aspects of this open call. As part of our selection process, applicants will have the option to provide information on gender, age, and socio-economic background. In the case of equal scores assigned to more than one applicant, the selection committee will prioritize female applicants, applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds, applicants experiencing disabilities, applicants from low DESI-countries, and applicants belonging to minority groups, in this order, ensuring a fair and balanced approach to admissions.

8.4. All information provided regarding gender, age, and social background will be collected voluntarily and treated confidentially in accordance with GDPR/Data Privacy regulations. These data will be used solely to inform our diversity monitoring and inclusive selection measures. 

9. Results notification 

Following the experts’ evaluation, all eligible applicants will be ranked according to their final assessment scores. Scholarships will be awarded based on this order of merit, beginning with the highest-ranked candidates. Successful applicants must confirm their acceptance of the formal scholarship offer within five (5) business days by replying to the University of Vaasa Open Call team at digime@uwasa.fi.

10. Redress process 

Applicants who are not satisfied with the evaluation of their application, may submit a written appeal within five (5) business days of receiving their result. Appeals will be reviewed by a panel, composed of two University of Vaasa DIGI-ME representatives, and one external member. All requests for appeal must be sent to the University of Vaasa DIGI-ME Open Call team at digime@uwasa.fi.  

11. Legal disclaimer

This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by the University of Vaasa. The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by the University of Vaasa in its own name and under its own responsibility. University of Vaasa’s own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants who will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim of increasing the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of the University of Vaasa.


Information pursuant to the European General Data Protection Regulation. The personal data of candidates and participants will be processed by the University of Vaasa for the purposes of DIGI-ME programme. These purposes involve the communication of data to bodies external to the University (EU Agencies, host institution), as required by current European legislation General Data Protection Regulation no. 2016/679 art. 13. For more information: https://it.uwasa.fi/dataprotection/.


[1] Students are regularly enrolled when they pay the tuition fees to the University of Vaasa by the set deadlines.
